before: Unsafe operations have conditions the programmer must uphold when the compiler cannot verify them. An unsafe block does not disable borrowing rules everywhere, make invalid memory valid or turn undefined behavior into a predictable demonstration. Safe public wrappers must enforce their own invariants before relying on unsafe internals.

slice.get returns an Option after checking the index, so this example needs no unsafe block at all. By contrast, get_unchecked requires a valid in-bounds index even if its result is not later used. We do not call it with an invalid index or execute any undefined-behavior example.
Expected output or behavior: missing. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Explain which precondition a safe wrapper would have to establish before any unchecked access; do not run an invalid example. You may trace it without a Rust compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: The safe get method gives a missing result when an index is outside an array.
The match reads a value only if it exists. An unchecked read would need a separate guarantee that the index is valid.
The output is `missing`. An array with two items has slots 0 and 1. Slot 3 is missing.
Follow the match for slot 1, which is inside the array.
